title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cf. previous page, diagram (21)). M~_{0,3} is an extended automorphism group of the profinite fundamental group of P^1-{0,1,∞}, with the outer quotient Π~. Through the isomorphism M'_{1,1} ≃ U_{0,3} (level-2 / Legendre structure), it maps via φ' to GL(2,Ẑ)' = GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}. The map comes from the action on the abelianized fundamental group of the corresponding once-punctured elliptic curve. The bottom row of (21) is reduction modulo the central ±1. N~_{1,1} is the unreduced version: pairs consisting of u ∈ N~_{0,3} and an honest matrix u_0 ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) lifting φ'(u).

The question on this page. Is there a privileged way to lift an element of GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 to GL(2,Ẑ)? Equivalently, can one normalise an element of N~_{1,1}, modulo composition with elements of SL(2,Z)^ (or modulo the sign), so that it satisfies a commutation property with the cusp generator σ_∞, say u(σ_∞) = ±σ_∞?

Reformulation. For the subgroup Π~_σ ⊂ M~_{0,3} (stabiliser data at the cusp σ), its image consists of Borel-type matrices u = μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞^α ∈ GL(2,Ẑ)^{(1)}, defined only up to sign. Does there exist a canonical section Π~_σ → N~_{1,1}, i.e. a canonical way to remove the sign ambiguity?

The 'yoga'. Replace Π~_σ by the Galois version Π_{Q,σ}. Then lifts should correspond to elliptic curves over Q with Jacobi level-2 rigidification lying over the rational point 1/2 of U_{0,3}(Q). This is completed on the next page: the choices form a torsor under H^1(Q,±1) = Hom(Γ_Q,±1), i.e. quadratic twists. That matches exactly the indeterminacy of lifting a projective GL2/±1 representation to GL2. So lifts exist (because such curves exist), but no choice is privileged, even over Γ_{Q,T}.

In modern terms: the obstruction and indeterminacy for lifting a Galois action from the coarse-moduli / rigidified level, where the elliptic involution is killed, to the full moduli stack M_{1,1} is the μ2-gerbe. Lifts are torsored by quadratic twists.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'normalisation' via u(σ_∞)=±σ_∞ alone cannot fix the sign, since -1 is central and commutes with σ_∞. This is consistent with the conclusion on the next page that no canonical choice exists.

The choice of base point 1/2 (λ=1/2, j=1728) is a convenient rational point. Any rational point gives the same twist-torsor picture, so the page's phrasing 'correspondant au point 1/2' is a choice, not a necessity.

ideas.what: Lifting the projective action GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 (coming from GT/Galois acting on π1 of P^1-{0,1,∞} via M_{1,1}[2] ≃ U_{0,3}) to an honest GL(2,Ẑ)-action; ambiguity from the central elliptic involution
ideas.modern_name: μ2-gerbe M_{1,1} → coarse/rigidified moduli; lifting GT or Galois actions from genus 0 to Γ_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (GT acting on Γ_{1,1}, late 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion of SL2-related groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only discusses the passage from M_{0,4} to M_{1,1} qualitatively

ideas.what: Lifts of Γ_Q → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 correspond to elliptic curves over Q with level-2 structure over a given rational point; indeterminacy H^1(Q,±1) = quadratic twists
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic twists as torsor of lifts; Galois action on Tate module of twisted Legendre curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (folklore in theory of elliptic curves)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames the sign problem in lifting the GT-type group Π~ (built from Ĝ_{0,3} data) to N~_{1,1}. He decides it via the 'yoga' that arithmetic sections correspond to rational points/curves, concluding that the lift is torsored by Hom(Γ_Q,±1) and is not canonical. This is a documented early instance of using the section-conjecture-style yoga to settle a GT/Γ_{1,1} lifting question.
missed.quote: y a-t-il un relèvement canonique Π~_σ → N~_{1,1} ... une façon de lever cette ambiguïté de signe ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it anticipates the later work of Nakamura–Schneps and Hain–Matsumoto on extending GT/Galois actions to genus 1, and the role of the central -1 there. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A thoughtful but essentially classical question, whose answer (quadratic-twist ambiguity) is standard. Its interest is historical, as an early pass at the genus-0 to genus-1 lifting of GT-type actions.
transcription_corrections: 'Sl(2,Z)^' is the profinite completion SL(2,Z)^ (i.e. SL(2,Ẑ)).
Line 6: the first alternative 'u(σ_∞)=εσ_∞' is crossed out or overwritten; the retained version is u(σ_∞)=±σ_∞.
'sous-groupes Π~_σ ⊂ M~_{0,3}': the image reads roughly 'Π~_σ ⊂ M~_{0,3}' (written with tilde), consistent with the transcription.
'GL(2,Ẑ)^{(1)}' may be a footnote mark (1) rather than a superscript index.
